```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 5,
  fig.height = 3,
  dpi = 96,
  dev = "png"
)
library(vellum)
```

vellum is the backend for a small ecosystem: [vellumplot](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/)
compiles a grammar of graphics *into* a vellum scene, and
[vellumwidget](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumwidget/) turns a rendered scene into an
interactive HTML widget. Both bind to a narrow seam: `scene_model()`,
`scene_svg()`, and the per-element metadata that rides on grobs. Above the
SVG-comfortable element count a host switches to a rasterised base layer, and
takes those pixels from `scene_png()` (raw bytes, no temp file) — part of the
same seam. Because the
three packages are version-locked and co-released, a change to that seam can
break the layers above it silently.

**This article is the authoritative description of that seam.** If you are
building on vellum, or changing vellum's output, this is the contract to hold
to. (It supersedes the internal design note `_docs/DESIGN-INTERACTIVITY.md`,
which is kept only as history.)

## The seam, in one picture

```
  vellumplot  ──compiles a plot to grobs carrying──▶  key / meta / id / role
                                                        │
  vellum  ──renders──▶  scene_svg()   (data-key, data-vellum-*, role attrs)
                        scene_model()  (per-element table: identity + bbox)
                        scene_png()    (raw PNG bytes, for the raster-base mode)
                                                        │
  vellumwidget  ──reads scene_svg() + scene_model()──▶  hover / select / brush / link
```

Everything below the grammar is *pure metadata*: a static PNG/SVG render never
calls `scene_model()`, and a grob without a `key`/`meta` still draws exactly as
before. Nothing here changes what is painted.

## Carrying identity on a grob

Eleven constructors take two optional identity arguments: the batched marks
`points_grob()`, `circle_grob()`, `rect_grob()`, `segments_grob()`,
`hexagon_grob()`, `sector_grob()`, `roundrect_grob()` and `text_grob()`, and the
single-shape marks `lines_grob()`, `polygon_grob()` and `path_grob()`.

- `key`: a character vector of **data keys**. This is the join key a host uses
  to tie an on-screen element back to a datum.
- `meta`: a list of **free-form per-element records**, e.g. a tooltip string or
  field values. It can also be given **columnar**: a data frame with one row
  per element and one column per field. Row `i` stands for the record of that
  row's values (a `NULL` entry in a list-column leaves its field out of the
  record), and it costs far less than a list of records when there are many
  elements.

On a batched mark both are per element and must have **length 1** (shared by
every element) **or exactly the element count**; any other length is an error
naming the argument, never a silent truncation or wrap. A single-shape mark is
one element, so it takes a single `key` and a single `meta` record.

Every grob also takes `id` and `role` (a single value per grob) for semantic
identity and accessibility. The remaining constructors (`bezier_grob()`,
`spline_grob()`, `loop_grob()`, `raster_grob()`, `svg_grob()`,
`text_path_grob()`, `contour_grob()`) take no `key` and never appear in the
tables below.

### Coordinates: bare numbers are npc

A bare number passed to any constructor's position or size argument is read in
`default_units`, which is `"npc"` (a fraction of the enclosing viewport)
everywhere, as in grid. A grammar layer placing data values inside a panel
viewport with an `xscale`/`yscale` must therefore say so, either with
`vl_unit(x, "native")` or `default_units = "native"`:

```{r}
#| label: native
panel <- vl_scene(3, 2, bg = "white") |>
  push(vl_viewport(name = "panel", xscale = c(0, 10), yscale = c(0, 100))) |>
  draw(points_grob(
    x = c(2, 5, 8),
    y = c(20, 80, 50),
    default_units = "native",
    key = c("a", "b", "c")
  )) |>
  pop()
panel
```

Arguments with a physical default keep it whatever `default_units` says: a bare
point, hexagon or loop `size`, `foot`, `start_cap`, `end_cap` and `offset` are
millimetres. Only the reading of *bare* numbers changes; a [vl_unit()] is never
reinterpreted.

```{r}
#| label: build
s <- vl_scene(5, 3, bg = "white") |>
  draw(points_grob(
    x    = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
    y    = c(0.4, 0.7, 0.4),
    size = vl_unit(6, "mm"),
    gp   = vl_gpar(fill = "#3498db", col = NA),
    key  = c("a", "b", "c"),
    meta = list(
      list(tooltip = "first"),
      list(tooltip = "second"),
      list(tooltip = "third")
    )
  ))
s
```

(Each batched grob carries one graphical style; the grammar layer above vellum
emits one grob per style bucket, so a scatter with three colours is three
`points_grob()`s. The `key`/`meta` machinery is per element regardless.)

## `scene_model()`: the per-element table

`scene_model()` walks the rendered scene and returns a list of **two data
frames**.

```{r}
#| label: model
m <- scene_model(s)
names(m)
```

### `elements`

One row per drawn element of the *keyable* marks, **in paint order**:

```{r}
#| label: elements
str(m$elements)
```

The columns are the contract:

| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | character | the data key (`NA` if the element was drawn without one) |
| `mark` | character | the mark kind (see vocabulary below) |
| `id` | character | the grob `id` (`NA` if unset) |
| `name` | character | the grob `name` (`NA` if unset) |
| `panel` | character | the innermost enclosing named viewport (`NA` if none) |
| `x0, y0, x1, y1` | numeric | device-pixel bounding box |
| `x, y` | numeric | element centre, `(x0+x1)/2, (y0+y1)/2` |
| `w, h` | numeric | element size, `x1-x0, y1-y0` |
| `meta` | list | the free-form per-element record (list-column; see below for the columnar form) |

`scene_model(scene, meta = "columns")` returns the same table with `meta` as a
**data-frame column** instead: one row per element and one column per field. A
field is a plain vector when every element carrying it holds one atomic value of
one type (`NA` for the elements without it), and a list-column (`NULL` where
absent) otherwise. A host that reads meta for many elements (vellumwidget does)
asks for this form, so no per-element record is ever built.

```{r}
#| label: model-columns
scene_model(s, meta = "columns")$elements$meta
```

The `mark` vocabulary is these eleven values, and only these:
`rect`, `point`, `circle`, `hexagon`, `sector`, `segment`, `roundrect`, `text`,
`path`, `line`, `polygon`. Adding one is a contract change (see the end of this
article).

Three families produce these rows:

- **Batched marks** (`rect`, `point`, `circle`, `hexagon`, `sector`, `segment`)
  emit **one row per element, always**, even when unkeyed (then `key` is `NA`).
- **Keyed-only batches** (`roundrect`, `text`) emit **one row per keyed
  element**. A grob drawn without `key` contributes no rows at all, and within a
  keyed grob an element whose key is `NA` or `""` is skipped. This keeps a
  plot's unkeyed axis labels and strip backgrounds out of the table.
- **Single-shape marks** (`path`, `line`, `polygon`) emit **one row per grob, and
  only when keyed**. An unkeyed path/line/polygon is geometry-only and does not
  appear in the table. (A single `sf` feature, one polygon or linestring, is
  exactly one such element.) Key one with the constructor's `key` argument
  (setting the grob's `@keys` slot is equivalent).

### `panels`

One row per **named panel** that encloses at least one row of `elements` (a
named viewport becomes an addressable panel; one with no elements in the table
has no row). An element's `panel` is its innermost enclosing named viewport.

```{r}
#| label: panels
str(m$panels)
```

Columns:

| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | character | the panel's viewport name |
| `x0, y0, x1, y1` | numeric | bounding box of the panel's *elements* (device px) |
| `px0, py0, px1, py1` | numeric | the panel viewport's **resolved device-px rectangle** — the true data region, from the layout solve, not just where marks landed (`NA` if the viewport was not captured) |
| `xscale_lo, xscale_hi` | numeric | the panel viewport's native x coordinate range (its `xscale`) |
| `yscale_lo, yscale_hi` | numeric | native y coordinate range (its `yscale`) |
| `meta` | list | the panel viewport's free-form `meta` (list-column; `NULL` when none) |

The pixel rectangle paired with the native range gives the affine that maps device
px ↔ native for that panel — the geometry a host needs to invert a pixel back to a
data coordinate. It is the panel-level analogue of an element's bbox + `meta`.

The panel-level `meta` (the `meta =` argument of [vl_viewport()]) is the same
opaque, host-read channel as element `meta`: vellum carries it untouched and names
no conventions. The grammar uses it for panel-scoped descriptors — e.g. the
`scales` descriptor `vellumplot` attaches to each data panel (per-axis type,
domain, breaks, and labels), which `vellumwidget` reads to map pixels back to data
values. That convention is documented by `vellumplot`, not here.

### The `meta` key vocabulary

vellum treats `meta` as opaque: it is a free-form list, recycled to the element
count and carried through untouched; vellum does **not** name or validate its
keys. The following key names are **conventions** the grammar (vellumplot) writes and
the widget (vellumwidget) reads. Documenting them here keeps the three layers in step;
they are not enforced by vellum.

| `meta` key | written by | read by | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tooltip` | vellumplot `tooltip=` | vellumwidget | hover tooltip text (falls back to `key`) |
| `data_id` | vellumplot `data_id=` | (becomes the `key`) | the data key for an element |
| `hover_group` | vellumplot `hover_group=` | vellumwidget | co-highlight a group on hover |
| `hover_color` | vellumplot mark aesthetic | vellumwidget | per-element hover outline colour |
| `selected_color` | vellumplot mark aesthetic | vellumwidget | per-element selection colour |
| `legend` | vellumplot legend keying | vellumwidget | the series a mark belongs to |
| `legend_for` | vellumplot legend keying | vellumwidget | the series a legend swatch drives (`"<aes>:<level>"`) |

If you add a convention, add it here.

## `element_geometry()`: the hit-test geometry

`scene_model()` gives boxes, which suit a rectangular brush and mislead for
anything diagonal, thin or holed. A host that hit-tests on the client (a browser
cannot call back into R on every mouse move) reads `element_geometry()` once
instead: the device-pixel geometry of every **keyed** element, recorded by the
same walk that renders the scene, so a segment drawn with an `offset` or end
caps is reported where it lands. `vl_nearest()` measures against exactly this
geometry, so a client that follows the rules below reproduces it.

```{r}
#| label: geometry
holed <- vl_scene(4, 3, dpi = 100) |>
  draw(path_grob(
    x = c(0.1, 0.9, 0.9, 0.1, 0.4, 0.6, 0.6, 0.4),
    y = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.9, 0.9, 0.4, 0.4, 0.6, 0.6),
    id = rep(1:2, each = 4),
    rule = "evenodd",
    key = "donut"
  ))
element_geometry(holed)
```

One row per vertex. The columns are the contract:

| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | character | the element's data key (repeated on each of its vertices) |
| `kind` | character | `segment`, `line`, `polygon`, `path`, `hexagon`, `sector`, `point`, `rect`, `roundrect`, `text` (a `circle_grob()` element reports as `point`) |
| `vertex` | integer | 1-based within the element; restarts at 1 for the next element |
| `ring` | integer | 1-based ring (or polyline) within the element |
| `x, y` | numeric | device px, y down |
| `rule` | character | the fill rule, per element: `"nonzero"`, `"evenodd"`, or `NA` for a kind with no interior (`segment`, `line`, `point`) |

The rules a client applies, which are the ones `vl_nearest()` applies:

- `segment` and `line` are open centre-lines: the distance is to the nearest
  edge, and an `NA` vertex is a break.
- `point` is a single centre; its radius is half the smaller side of its
  `scene_model()` box.
- `rect` and `roundrect` are two opposite box corners, filled as `"nonzero"`.
- Everything else (`polygon`, `path`, `hexagon`, `sector`, and a `text` label's
  box) is closed rings. **Containment is decided once, across all
  of an element's rings, under its `rule`**: even-odd parity of the edge
  crossings, or a nonzero sum of the rings' winding numbers. Inside is distance
  zero. Outside -- and a point in a hole is outside -- the distance is to the
  nearest edge of any ring. Rings are never joined: each closes on itself.

`rule` comes from the grob: `path_grob(rule = "evenodd")` reports `"evenodd"`,
and `rule = "winding"` (the default) and every other filled kind report
`"nonzero"`. `vl_nearest()` and `hit_test()` both decide containment by that
rule, so a click in the hole of an even-odd path is outside it, and `hit_test()`
falls through to whatever is drawn beneath:

```{r}
#| label: hole
vl_nearest(holed, 0.5, 0.5)$dist # in the hole: outside, so a positive distance
vl_nearest(holed, 0.2, 0.5)$dist # in the ring: inside
is.null(hit_test(holed, 0.5, 0.5)) # nothing under the hole
```

## `scene_svg()`: the emitted attributes

`scene_svg()` returns the same scene as an SVG string. Interactivity rides on SVG
attributes; the raster and PDF backends ignore all of them.

```{r}
#| label: svg
svg <- scene_svg(s)
# the data-key attributes on the three points:
regmatches(svg, gregexpr('data-key="[^"]*"', svg))[[1]]
```

Six attributes, each emitted only when its source is set:

| attribute | source | scope | set from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-key` | grob `key` | per element | `points_grob(key=)` etc. (every constructor that takes `key`) |
| `data-vellum-id` | grob `id` | per grob/node | `*_grob(id=)` |
| `data-vellum-name` | grob `name` | per grob/node | `*_grob(name=)` |
| `role` | grob `role` | per grob/node | `*_grob(role=)` |
| `data-vellum-panel` | named viewport | wrapping `<g>` | `vl_viewport(name=)` |
| `data-vellum-pan` | pannable panel's inner group | inner `<g>` | `vl_viewport(pannable=)` |

An empty/`NULL` source emits **no attribute**, so a scene that declares no
interactivity is byte-for-byte identical to one built before any of this existed.

### Pannable panels

A named viewport marked `vl_viewport(pannable = TRUE)` is emitted as **two nested
groups** instead of one: an outer `<g data-vellum-panel="name">` that carries the
panel's clip (untransformed, so the clip region stays fixed) around an inner
`<g data-vellum-pan="name">` holding the content. The panel's clip is **hoisted
once** to the outer group (rather than repeated per element), so a host can set a
`transform` on the inner group to pan/zoom the marks while the clip — and the
axes/legend outside the panel — stay put. This is the structural basis for
host-side axis-aware zoom. It is SVG-only and inert for static rendering (the
extra group has no transform until a host sets one); non-pannable panels and other
backends are unchanged.

## Split rendering for hosts

A host that draws many marks does not want them all as SVG elements. vellumwidget
splits a scene into layers instead: the furniture (background, gridlines, axes,
legends) as SVG, and the keyed marks as a PNG, or drawn by the browser itself
from a display list. Every layer is drawn on the same page, with the same
transforms and clips, so the layers overlay pixel for pixel.

### `layer =` in `scene_svg()` and `scene_png()`

| `layer` | draws |
|---|---|
| `"all"` (default) | the whole scene |
| `"keyed"` | only the marks with a `key`, on a transparent page |
| `"unkeyed"` | everything else |
| `"unkeyed_below"` | the unkeyed elements painted before the marks |
| `"unkeyed_above"` | the unkeyed elements painted after the marks, on a transparent page |
| `"keyed_flagged"` | only the keyed marks the display list cannot draw exactly (see below), on a transparent page |

`"keyed"` over `"unkeyed"` reproduces the full render, except that an unkeyed
element painted *after* a mark ends up under it. Stacking `"unkeyed_below"`,
`"keyed"` and `"unkeyed_above"` keeps that order too. In this scene the dashed
reference line is drawn after the points, so it belongs to the top layer:

```{r}
#| label: split
#| fig.width: 6
#| fig.height: 1.5
split <- vl_scene(3, 1.8, dpi = 96, bg = "white") |>
  push(vl_viewport(name = "panel", xscale = c(0, 10), yscale = c(0, 10))) |>
  draw(rect_grob(gp = vl_gpar(fill = "grey93", col = NA))) |>
  draw(points_grob(vl_unit(c(2, 5, 8), "native"), vl_unit(c(3, 6, 4), "native"),
                   size = vl_unit(6, "mm"), key = c("a", "b", "c"),
                   gp = vl_gpar(fill = "#2c6fa6", col = NA))) |>
  draw(segments_grob(0, vl_unit(5, "native"), 1, vl_unit(5, "native"),
                     gp = vl_gpar(col = "#c0392b", lwd = 2, lty = "dashed"))) |>
  pop()

layers <- c("unkeyed_below", "keyed", "unkeyed_above", "all")
files <- vapply(layers, function(l) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  writeBin(scene_png(split, layer = l), f)
  f
}, character(1))

sheet <- vl_scene(6, 1.5, dpi = 96, bg = "white")
for (i in seq_along(files)) {
  sheet <- sheet |>
    draw(rect_grob(x = (i - 0.5) / 4, y = 0.6, width = vl_unit(1.2, "in"),
                   height = vl_unit(0.72, "in"),
                   gp = vl_gpar(fill = "#ffe9e9", col = "grey70"))) |>
    draw(raster_grob(files[i], x = (i - 0.5) / 4, y = 0.6,
                     width = vl_unit(1.2, "in"), height = vl_unit(0.72, "in"))) |>
    draw(text_grob(layers[i], x = (i - 0.5) / 4, y = 0.08,
                   gp = vl_gpar(fontsize = 9)))
}
display(sheet)
```

The pink behind the second and third layers is the transparent page showing
through. `panels =` narrows the mark layer to keyed marks in the named panels,
so a legend's keyed swatches can stay with the furniture; the layers stay exact
complements.

### The display list

`scene_display_list()` resolves every keyed mark to device-pixel geometry, a
paint and its key, packed as compact columns that a browser draws and hit-tests
without parsing SVG. It is **internal but versioned**: it is a private vellum to
vellumwidget payload, documented in `?scene_display_list` but not a format to
build on. Its fields may change in any release, in step with vellumwidget, and
`version =` says which layout the reader gets. A reader that knows only
version 1 must never be handed version 2.

```{r}
#| label: display-list
dl <- scene_display_list(split, version = 2, precision = "u16")
dl$format
unlist(dl[c("version", "n", "runs")])
dl$keys
```

`version = 2` adds linear and radial gradient fills with `pad` extension, clips
by a path, and opacity groups to what the list draws exactly. `precision` quantises the coordinates to 16 or 24 bits
(or to a largest rounding error in device px), and `keys` lets a host that
already holds the keys avoid shipping them twice.

Some marks cannot be drawn from the list: a mark under a mask, a blend mode or
an effect, a pattern fill, a repeating or reflecting gradient, a gradient
stroke, or text. A `vl_hatch()` fill is mostly not among them: vellum expands
it into the shape, filled with the hatch's background, and a path of its rules,
and lists both exactly. Only a hatched point marker other than a circle is
flagged, since its single point record cannot carry the rules. The list still carries the others, for hit-testing, but
flags them, and groups them into numbered **runs**: stretches of flagged marks
in paint order that no exactly drawn mark interrupts.
`scene_png(layer = "keyed_flagged", run = k)` draws run `k` alone, so the host
composites it at its place in paint order (`run_blend` gives the
blend mode to composite with):

```{r}
#| label: flagged
dots <- circle_grob(r = 0.3, gp = vl_gpar(fill = "#2c6fa6", col = NA))
flagged <- split |>
  draw(rect_grob(x = 0.8, y = 0.75, width = 0.25, height = 0.3, key = "p",
                 gp = vl_gpar(fill = vl_pattern(dots, width = 0.05, height = 0.08))))
fl <- scene_display_list(flagged, version = 2)
fl$runs
length(scene_png(flagged, layer = "keyed_flagged", run = 1)) > 0
```

### `vellum_content_fit`

A guest scene whose content has a fixed aspect ratio (a map, or a plot with a
fixed coordinate ratio) can declare it with the attribute
`vellum_content_fit`: `c(fixed_w, fixed_h, null_w, null_h)`, the fixed width
and height of its frame in mm and the weights of its aspect-locked `null`
tracks. vellumplot sets it on an aspect-locked plot. `scene_inset(fit = "auto")`
reads it and shrinks the inset's region around the content, so its background
and border hug the plot (see `vignette("scenes-as-values")`). The attribute,
like the display list, is part of the contract between the packages.

## Accessibility

A scene carries an optional accessible **name** and **description**, set with
`vl_scene(title=, desc=)` or `describe(scene, title=, desc=)`. When present:

- the **SVG** root becomes `<svg role="img" aria-labelledby="…">` with `<title>`
  and `<desc>` children (the reliable screen-reader pattern; WCAG 1.1.1);
- the **PDF** is a **tagged PDF**: the chart is a `Figure` in the structure tree
  whose `Alt` is the description.
- the **PowerPoint** group holding the scene carries the description (or the
  title, when there is no description) as its alt text, and is named after the
  title when written by `render()` or `pptx_pages()` (through officer it takes
  the placeholder's name).

This is additive: with no title/desc the output is unchanged. The grammar layer
(`vellumplot`) sets these automatically from the plot's title and an auto-generated (or
`labs(alt=)`) alt text. See vellumplot's [Accessibility
article](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/articles/accessibility.html).
Per-element `role` (above) is a genuine ARIA role; the interactive widget layer
(`vellumwidget`) adds
keyboard navigation and live-region announcements on top.

## Invariants the contract guarantees

These are the properties vellumplot and vellumwidget are entitled to rely on, and that
vellum's own tests (`tests/testthat/test-contract.R`) pin down:

1. **Paint order.** `scene_model()$elements` is in draw order, and the SVG emits
   elements in the same order. A host can zip the SVG DOM and the table
   positionally.
2. **Semantic/geometry agreement.** `scene_model()` builds the identity columns
   from the R grob tree and the geometry columns from the compiled backend, then
   asserts they enumerate the same elements: the element counts must match and
   the `key` column must be identical at every position. A mismatch is a hard
   error (a compiler bug), never a silent mis-join.
3. **Additivity.** `key`/`meta`/`id`/`role` never change what is drawn. A render
   with no keys is identical to the same scene without the machinery, on every
   backend.
4. **Stable `id` join key.** A grob's `id` surfaces as `data-vellum-id` in the
   SVG *and* is the join key vellumplot records in its provenance table, so a widget
   can map an SVG node to the grammar record that produced it.

## For contributors

If you change any of the following, update this article and the contract tests
in the same commit, and expect to co-release vellumplot and vellumwidget:

- the `elements`/`panels` column set or types,
- the `element_geometry()` column set, its `kind` and `rule` vocabularies, or
  the containment rule above,
- the `mark` vocabulary,
- which marks are keyable, or the batched / keyed-only / single-shape rules,
- the `key`/`meta` length rule (1 or the element count),
- the default reading of bare numbers (`default_units = "npc"`),
- the SVG attribute names, or when they are emitted,
- the `layer` values of `scene_svg()` / `scene_png()`, the display-list format
  (bump its `version`), or the `vellum_content_fit` attribute,
- the reserved `meta` key vocabulary.
```
